PRE-LAUNCH PREVIEW · CONTENT & INTEGRATIONS IN REVIEW
HOW WE ENGAGE

The right shape
for the work.

Start with the problem, the people and the decision to be made. Then choose an engagement that makes delivery clear.

01 / ENGAGEMENT

Audit

When you need to know what to fix first.

A focused review of the evidence, the experience and the constraints. We define the questions, inspect agreed systems and deliver a prioritized set of recommendations.

  • Documented baseline
  • Findings with evidence
  • Prioritized next steps

[Owner to confirm: audit scope, turnaround, fee and presentation format.]

02 / ENGAGEMENT

Project

When there is a defined outcome to deliver.

A bounded engagement for a website, product release, campaign setup or measurement implementation. Scope, dependencies and acceptance criteria are agreed before delivery.

  • Delivery plan and milestones
  • Working reviews and QA evidence
  • Handover documentation

[Owner to confirm: milestone/payment structure, change control and support period.]

03 / ENGAGEMENT

Retainer

When improvement needs a consistent rhythm.

A rolling backlog of priorities across acquisition, content, analytics or optimization. Capacity and review cadence are agreed so the work stays connected to business needs.

  • Prioritized monthly backlog
  • Reporting and decisions
  • Regular planning review

[Owner to confirm: capacity, term, reporting cadence and cancellation terms.]

04 / ENGAGEMENT

Embedded team

When your team needs additional delivery capacity.

Work alongside internal product, marketing or engineering teams with clear ownership. Agree decision rights, access and delivery responsibilities before work begins.

  • Shared working agreements
  • Integrated planning and reviews
  • Documented knowledge transfer

[Owner to confirm: roles, allocation, availability and escalation contacts.]

Governance belongs
in the scope.

A visible delivery rhythm.

Agree sprint length, review meetings, owners and reporting cadence at kickoff. Keep decisions and dependencies in a shared record.

Quality before release.

Define acceptance criteria and appropriate functional, performance, accessibility and security checks. Record known issues and release decisions.

Clear support boundaries.

Service hours, response targets, escalation paths and any SLAs belong in the signed agreement. No universal service level is implied here.

[Owner to approve: governance defaults and contractual templates before offering engagements.]
